### <a name="nitro_server"></a>`nitro_server`

Configuration for server resource. Attributes map 1:1 onto the NITRO `server` API, see the NITRO reference.
 Only attributes set in the manifest are managed.

The title is the NITRO `name`.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `nitro_server` type.

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Any information about the server.

##### `domain`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Domain name of the server. For a domain based configuration, you must create the server first.

##### `domainresolveretry`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[5, 20939]]`

Time, in seconds, for which the NetScaler must wait, after DNS resolution fails, before sending the next DNS query to resolve the domain name.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this resource should be present or absent on the NetScaler.

Default value: `present`

##### `ipaddress`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

IPv4 or IPv6 address of the server. If you create an IP address based server, you can specify the name of the server, instead of its IP address, when creating a service. Note: If you do not create a server entry, the server IP address that you enter when you create a service becomes the name of the server.

##### `ipv6address`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Support IPv6 addressing mode. If you configure a server with the IPv6 addressing mode, you cannot use the server in the IPv4 addressing mode.

##### `querytype`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['A', 'AAAA', 'SRV']]`

Specify the type of DNS resolution to be done on the configured domain to get the backend services. Valid query types are A, AAAA and SRV with A being the default querytype. The type of DNS resolution done on the domains in SRV records is inherited from ipv6 argument.

##### `state`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

Initial state of the server.

##### `td`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[0, 4094]]`

Integer value that uniquely identifies the traffic domain in which you want to configure the entity. If you do not specify an ID, the entity becomes part of the default traffic domain, which has an ID of 0.

##### `translationip`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

IP address used to transform the server's DNS-resolved IP address.

##### `translationmask`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

The netmask of the translation ip

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `nitro_server` type.

* [`delay`](#-nitro_server--delay)
* [`domainresolvenow`](#-nitro_server--domainresolvenow)
* [`graceful`](#-nitro_server--graceful)
* [`name`](#-nitro_server--name)

##### <a name="-nitro_server--delay"></a>`delay`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Time, in seconds, after which all the services configured on the server are disabled.

##### <a name="-nitro_server--domainresolvenow"></a>`domainresolvenow`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Immediately send a DNS query to resolve the server's domain name.

##### <a name="-nitro_server--graceful"></a>`graceful`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Shut down gracefully, without accepting any new connections, and disabling each service when all of its connections are
closed.

##### <a name="-nitro_server--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `String`

Name for the server.\nMust begin with an ASCII alphabetic or underscore (_) character, and must contain only ASCII
alphanumeric, underscore, hash (#), period (.), space, colon (:), at (@), equals (=), and hyphen (-) characters.\nCan be
changed after the name is created.

### <a name="nitro_service"></a>`nitro_service`

Configuration for service resource. Attributes map 1:1 onto the NITRO `service` API, see the NITRO reference.
 Only attributes set in the manifest are managed.

The title is the NITRO `name`.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `nitro_service` type.

##### `accessdown`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Use Layer 2 mode to bridge the packets sent to this service if it is marked as DOWN. If the service is DOWN, and this parameter is disabled, the packets are dropped.

##### `aigwprofilename`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of the AIGW Profile that contains AIGW Endpoint setting for the service.

##### `appflowlog`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

Enable logging of AppFlow information.

##### `cacheable`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Use the transparent cache redirection virtual server to forward requests to the cache server.\nNote: Do not specify this parameter if you set the Cache Type parameter.

##### `cachetype`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['TRANSPARENT', 'REVERSE', 'FORWARD']]`

Cache type supported by the cache server.

##### `cip`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

Before forwarding a request to the service, insert an HTTP header with the client's IPv4 or IPv6 address as its value. Used if the server needs the client's IP address for security, accounting, or other purposes, and setting the Use Source IP parameter is not a viable option.

##### `cipheader`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name for the HTTP header whose value must be set to the IP address of the client. Used with the Client IP parameter. If you set the Client IP parameter, and you do not specify a name for the header, the appliance uses the header name specified for the global Client IP Header parameter (the cipHeader parameter in the set ns param CLI command or the Client IP Header parameter in the Configure HTTP Parameters dialog box at System > Settings > Change HTTP parameters). If the global Client IP Header parameter is not specified, the appliance inserts a header with the name \"client-ip.\"

##### `cka`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Enable client keep-alive for the service.

##### `cleartextport`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[1]]`

Port to which clear text data must be sent after the appliance decrypts incoming SSL traffic. Applicable to transparent SSL services.

##### `clttimeout`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[0, 31536000]]`

Time, in seconds, after which to terminate an idle client connection.

##### `cmp`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Enable compression for the service.

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Any information about the service.

##### `contentinspectionprofilename`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of the ContentInspection profile that contains IPS/IDS communication related setting for the service

##### `customserverid`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Unique identifier for the service. Used when the persistency type for the virtual server is set to Custom Server ID.

##### `dnsprofilename`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of the DNS profile to be associated with the service. DNS profile properties will applied to the transactions processed by a service. This parameter is valid only for ADNS, ADNS-TCP and ADNS-DOT services.

##### `downstateflush`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

Flush all active transactions associated with a service whose state transitions from UP to DOWN. Do not enable this option for applications that must complete their transactions.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this resource should be present or absent on the NetScaler.

Default value: `present`

##### `hashid`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[1]]`

A numerical identifier that can be used by hash based load balancing methods. Must be unique for each service.

##### `healthmonitor`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Monitor the health of this service. Available settings function as follows:\nYES - Send probes to check the health of the service.\nNO - Do not send probes to check the health of the service. With the NO option, the appliance shows the service as UP at all times.

##### `httpprofilename`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of the HTTP profile that contains HTTP configuration settings for the service.

##### `ipaddress`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

The new IP address of the service.

##### `maxbandwidth`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[0, 4294967287]]`

Maximum bandwidth, in Kbps, allocated to the service.

##### `maxclient`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[0, 4294967294]]`

Maximum number of simultaneous open connections to the service.

##### `maxreq`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[0, 65535]]`

Maximum number of requests that can be sent on a persistent connection to the service.\nNote: Connection requests beyond this value are rejected.

##### `mcpprofilename`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of MCP profile which will be attached to the service.

##### `monconnectionclose`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['RESET', 'FIN']]`

Close monitoring connections by sending the service a connection termination message with the specified bit set.

##### `monthreshold`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[0, 65535]]`

Minimum sum of weights of the monitors that are bound to this service. Used to determine whether to mark a service as UP or DOWN.

##### `netprofile`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Network profile to use for the service.

##### `pathmonitor`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Path monitoring for clustering

##### `pathmonitorindv`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Individual Path monitoring decisions

##### `port`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[1, 65535]]`

Port number of the service.

##### `processlocal`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

By turning on this option packets destined to a service in a cluster will not under go any steering. Turn this option for single packet request response mode or when the upstream device is performing a proper RSS for connection based distribution.

##### `quicprofilename`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of QUIC profile which will be attached to the service.

##### `rtspsessionidremap`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ON', 'OFF']]`

Enable RTSP session ID mapping for the service.

##### `serverid`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

The  identifier for the service. This is used when the persistency type is set to Custom Server ID.

##### `servername`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of the server that hosts the service.

##### `servicetype`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['HTTP', 'FTP', 'TCP', 'UDP', 'SSL', 'SSL_BRIDGE', 'SSL_TCP', 'DTLS', 'NNTP', 'RPCSVR', 'DNS', 'ADNS', 'SNMP', 'RTSP', 'DHCPRA', 'ANY', 'SIP_UDP', 'SIP_TCP', 'SIP_SSL', 'DNS_TCP', 'ADNS_TCP', 'MYSQL', 'MSSQL', 'ORACLE', 'MONGO', 'MONGO_TLS', 'RADIUS', 'RADIUSListener', 'RDP', 'DIAMETER', 'SSL_DIAMETER', 'TFTP', 'SMPP', 'PPTP', 'GRE', 'SYSLOGTCP', 'SYSLOGUDP', 'FIX', 'SSL_FIX', 'USER_TCP', 'USER_SSL_TCP', 'QUIC', 'IPFIX', 'LOGSTREAM', 'LOGSTREAM_SSL', 'MQTT', 'MQTT_TLS', 'QUIC_BRIDGE', 'DOT', 'ADNS_DOT', 'HTTP_QUIC', 'ADNS_DOH', 'KAFKA_BROKER']]`

Protocol in which data is exchanged with the service.

##### `sp`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ON', 'OFF']]`

Enable surge protection for the service.

##### `state`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

Initial state of the service.

##### `svrtimeout`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[0, 31536000]]`

Time, in seconds, after which to terminate an idle server connection.

##### `tcpb`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Enable TCP buffering for the service.

##### `tcpprofilename`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of the TCP profile that contains TCP configuration settings for the service.

##### `td`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[0, 4094]]`

Integer value that uniquely identifies the traffic domain in which you want to configure the entity. If you do not specify an ID, the entity becomes part of the default traffic domain, which has an ID of 0.

##### `useproxyport`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Use the proxy port as the source port when initiating connections with the server. With the NO setting, the client-side connection port is used as the source port for the server-side connection.\nNote: This parameter is available only when the Use Source IP (USIP) parameter is set to YES.

##### `usip`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Use the client's IP address as the source IP address when initiating a connection to the server. When creating a service, if you do not set this parameter, the service inherits the global Use Source IP setting (available in the enable ns mode and disable ns mode CLI commands, or in the System > Settings > Configure modes > Configure Modes dialog box). However, you can override this setting after you create the service.

##### `wasmmodule`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of the WASM module to bind to this service.

##### `weight`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[1, 100]]`

Weight to assign to the monitor-service binding. When a monitor is UP, the weight assigned to its binding with the service determines how much the monitor contributes toward keeping the health of the service above the value configured for the Monitor Threshold parameter.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `nitro_service` type.

* [`delay`](#-nitro_service--delay)
* [`graceful`](#-nitro_service--graceful)
* [`ip`](#-nitro_service--ip)
* [`monitor_name_svc`](#-nitro_service--monitor_name_svc)
* [`name`](#-nitro_service--name)

##### <a name="-nitro_service--delay"></a>`delay`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Time, in seconds, allocated to the NetScaler for a graceful shutdown of the service. During this period, new requests
are sent to the service only for clients who already have persistent sessions on the appliance. Requests from new
clients are load balanced among other available services. After the delay time expires, no requests are sent to the
service, and the service is marked as unavailable (OUT OF SERVICE).

##### <a name="-nitro_service--graceful"></a>`graceful`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Shut down gracefully, not accepting any new connections, and disabling the service when all of its connections are
closed.

##### <a name="-nitro_service--ip"></a>`ip`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

IP to assign to the service.

##### <a name="-nitro_service--monitor_name_svc"></a>`monitor_name_svc`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of the monitor bound to the specified service.

##### <a name="-nitro_service--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `String`

Name for the service. Must begin with an ASCII alphabetic or underscore (_) character, and must contain only ASCII
alphanumeric, underscore, hash (#), period (.), space, colon (:), at (@), equals (=), and hyphen (-) characters. Cannot
be changed after the service has been created.

### <a name="nitro_service_lbmonitor_binding"></a>`nitro_service_lbmonitor_binding`

Binding Resource definition for describing association between service and lbmonitor resources Attributes map 1:1 onto the NITRO `service_lbmonitor_binding` API, see the NITRO reference.
 Only attributes set in the manifest are managed.

The title is split into `name`, `monitor_name`.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `nitro_service_lbmonitor_binding` type.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this resource should be present or absent on the NetScaler.

Default value: `present`

##### `monstate`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

The configured state (enable/disable) of the monitor on this server.

##### `passive`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Indicates if load monitor is passive. A passive load monitor does not remove service from LB decision when threshold is breached.

##### `weight`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[1, 100]]`

Weight to assign to the monitor-service binding. When a monitor is UP, the weight assigned to its binding with the service determines how much the monitor contributes toward keeping the health of the service above the value configured for the Monitor Threshold parameter.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `nitro_service_lbmonitor_binding` type.

* [`monitor_name`](#-nitro_service_lbmonitor_binding--monitor_name)
* [`name`](#-nitro_service_lbmonitor_binding--name)

##### <a name="-nitro_service_lbmonitor_binding--monitor_name"></a>`monitor_name`

namevar

Data type: `String`

The monitor Names.

##### <a name="-nitro_service_lbmonitor_binding--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `String`

Name of the service to which to bind a monitor.

### <a name="nitro_servicegroup"></a>`nitro_servicegroup`

Configuration for service group resource. Attributes map 1:1 onto the NITRO `servicegroup` API, see the NITRO reference.
 Only attributes set in the manifest are managed.

The title is the NITRO `servicegroupname`.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `nitro_servicegroup` type.

##### `aigwprofilename`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of the backend AIGW Profile which will be attached to the servicegroup. This parameter enables the servicegroup to process the LLM request/response based on the profile config. Any service item bound to the servicegroup will inherit the backend AIGW Profile bound at the servicegroup level, if it does not have an explicit AIGW Profile given at bind time.

##### `appflowlog`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

Enable logging of AppFlow information for the specified service group.

##### `autodelayedtrofs`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Indicates graceful movement of IP-Port binding/s to TROFS when IP addresses are removed from DNS response. System will wait for monitor response timeout period before moving to TROFS .

##### `autodisabledelay`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

The time allowed (in seconds) for a graceful shutdown. During this period, new connections or requests will continue to be sent to this service for clients who already have a persistent session on the system. Connections or requests from fresh or new clients who do not yet have a persistence sessions on the system will not be sent to the service. Instead, they will be load balanced among other available services. After the delay time expires, no new requests or connections will be sent to the service.

##### `autodisablegraceful`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Indicates graceful shutdown of the service. System will wait for all outstanding connections to this service to be closed before disabling the service.

##### `autoscale`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['DISABLED', 'DNS', 'POLICY', 'CLOUD', 'API']]`

Auto scale option for a servicegroup

##### `bootstrap`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Flag to check if kafka broker servicegroup is of type bootstrap or not.

##### `cacheable`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Use the transparent cache redirection virtual server to forward the request to the cache server.\nNote: Do not set this parameter if you set the Cache Type.

##### `cachetype`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['TRANSPARENT', 'REVERSE', 'FORWARD']]`

Cache type supported by the cache server.

##### `cip`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

Insert the Client IP header in requests forwarded to the service.

##### `cipheader`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of the HTTP header whose value must be set to the IP address of the client. Used with the Client IP parameter. If client IP insertion is enabled, and the client IP header is not specified, the value of Client IP Header parameter or the value set by the set ns config command is used as client's IP header name.

##### `cka`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Enable client keep-alive for the service group.

##### `clttimeout`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[0, 31536000]]`

Time, in seconds, after which to terminate an idle client connection.

##### `cmp`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Enable compression for the specified service.

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Any information about the service group.

##### `customserverid`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

The identifier for this IP:Port pair. Used when the persistency type is set to Custom Server ID.

##### `dbsttl`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Specify the TTL for DNS record for domain based service.The default value of ttl is 0 which indicates to use the TTL received in DNS response for monitors

##### `downstateflush`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

Flush all active transactions associated with all the services in the service group whose state transitions from UP to DOWN. Do not enable this option for applications that must complete their transactions.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this resource should be present or absent on the NetScaler.

Default value: `present`

##### `hashid`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[1]]`

The hash identifier for the service. This must be unique for each service. This parameter is used by hash based load balancing methods.

##### `healthmonitor`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Monitor the health of this service.  Available settings function as follows:\nYES - Send probes to check the health of the service.\nNO - Do not send probes to check the health of the service. With the NO option, the appliance shows the service as UP at all times.

##### `httpprofilename`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of the HTTP profile that contains HTTP configuration settings for the service group.

##### `maxbandwidth`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[0, 4294967287]]`

Maximum bandwidth, in Kbps, allocated for all the services in the service group.

##### `maxclient`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[0, 4294967294]]`

Maximum number of simultaneous open connections for the service group.

##### `maxreq`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[0, 65535]]`

Maximum number of requests that can be sent on a persistent connection to the service group.\nNote: Connection requests beyond this value are rejected.

##### `mcpprofilename`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of MCP profile which will be attached to the servicegroup.

##### `memberport`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

member port

##### `monconnectionclose`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['RESET', 'FIN']]`

Close monitoring connections by sending the service a connection termination message with the specified bit set.

##### `monthreshold`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[0, 65535]]`

Minimum sum of weights of the monitors that are bound to this service. Used to determine whether to mark a service as UP or DOWN.

##### `nameserver`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Specify the nameserver to which the query for bound domain needs to be sent. If not specified, use the global nameserver

##### `netprofile`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Network profile for the service group.

##### `order`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[1, 8192]]`

Order number to be assigned to the servicegroup member

##### `pathmonitor`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Path monitoring for clustering

##### `pathmonitorindv`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Individual Path monitoring decisions.

##### `port`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[1, 65535]]`

Server port number.

##### `quicprofilename`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of QUIC profile which will be attached to the service group.

##### `rtspsessionidremap`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ON', 'OFF']]`

Enable RTSP session ID mapping for the service group.

##### `serverid`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

The  identifier for the service. This is used when the persistency type is set to Custom Server ID.

##### `servername`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of the server to which to bind the service group.

##### `servicetype`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['HTTP', 'FTP', 'TCP', 'UDP', 'SSL', 'SSL_BRIDGE', 'SSL_TCP', 'DTLS', 'NNTP', 'RPCSVR', 'DNS', 'ADNS', 'SNMP', 'RTSP', 'DHCPRA', 'ANY', 'SIP_UDP', 'SIP_TCP', 'SIP_SSL', 'DNS_TCP', 'ADNS_TCP', 'MYSQL', 'MSSQL', 'ORACLE', 'MONGO', 'MONGO_TLS', 'RADIUS', 'RADIUSListener', 'RDP', 'DIAMETER', 'SSL_DIAMETER', 'TFTP', 'SMPP', 'PPTP', 'GRE', 'SYSLOGTCP', 'SYSLOGUDP', 'FIX', 'SSL_FIX', 'USER_TCP', 'USER_SSL_TCP', 'QUIC', 'IPFIX', 'LOGSTREAM', 'LOGSTREAM_SSL', 'MQTT', 'MQTT_TLS', 'QUIC_BRIDGE', 'DOT', 'ADNS_DOT', 'HTTP_QUIC', 'ADNS_DOH', 'KAFKA_BROKER']]`

Protocol used to exchange data with the service.

##### `sp`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ON', 'OFF']]`

Enable surge protection for the service group.

##### `state`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

Initial state of the service group.

##### `svrtimeout`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[0, 31536000]]`

Time, in seconds, after which to terminate an idle server connection.

##### `tcpb`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Enable TCP buffering for the service group.

##### `tcpprofilename`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of the TCP profile that contains TCP configuration settings for the service group.

##### `td`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[0, 4094]]`

Integer value that uniquely identifies the traffic domain in which you want to configure the entity. If you do not specify an ID, the entity becomes part of the default traffic domain, which has an ID of 0.

##### `topicname`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of the Kafka topic.

##### `useproxyport`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Use the proxy port as the source port when initiating connections with the server. With the NO setting, the client-side connection port is used as the source port for the server-side connection.\nNote: This parameter is available only when the Use Source IP (USIP) parameter is set to YES.

##### `usip`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Use client's IP address as the source IP address when initiating connection to the server. With the NO setting, which is the default, a mapped IP (MIP) address or subnet IP (SNIP) address is used as the source IP address to initiate server side connections.

##### `wasmmodule`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of the WASM module to bind to this service.

##### `weight`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[1, 100]]`

Weight to assign to the servers in the service group. Specifies the capacity of the servers relative to the other servers in the load balancing configuration. The higher the weight, the higher the percentage of requests sent to the service.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `nitro_servicegroup` type.

* [`delay`](#-nitro_servicegroup--delay)
* [`dup_weight`](#-nitro_servicegroup--dup_weight)
* [`graceful`](#-nitro_servicegroup--graceful)
* [`monitor_name_svc`](#-nitro_servicegroup--monitor_name_svc)
* [`name`](#-nitro_servicegroup--name)

##### <a name="-nitro_servicegroup--delay"></a>`delay`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Time, in seconds, allocated for a shutdown of the services in the service group. During this period, new requests are
sent to the service only for clients who already have persistent sessions on the appliance. Requests from new clients
are load balanced among other available services. After the delay time expires, no requests are sent to the service, and
the service is marked as unavailable (OUT OF SERVICE).

##### <a name="-nitro_servicegroup--dup_weight"></a>`dup_weight`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[1]]`

weight of the monitor that is bound to servicegroup.

##### <a name="-nitro_servicegroup--graceful"></a>`graceful`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Wait for all existing connections to the service to terminate before shutting down the service.

##### <a name="-nitro_servicegroup--monitor_name_svc"></a>`monitor_name_svc`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of the monitor bound to the service group. Used to assign a weight to the monitor.

##### <a name="-nitro_servicegroup--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `String`

Name of the service group. Must begin with an ASCII alphabetic or underscore (_) character, and must contain only ASCII
alphanumeric, underscore, hash (#), period (.), space, colon (:), at (@), equals (=), and hyphen (-) characters. Can be
changed after the name is created. (NITRO: `servicegroupname`)

### <a name="nitro_servicegroup_lbmonitor_binding"></a>`nitro_servicegroup_lbmonitor_binding`

Binding Resource definition for describing association between servicegroup and lbmonitor resources Attributes map 1:1 onto the NITRO `servicegroup_lbmonitor_binding` API, see the NITRO reference.
 Only attributes set in the manifest are managed.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `nitro_servicegroup_lbmonitor_binding` type.

##### `aigwprofilename`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of the backend AIGW Profile which will be attached to the servicegroup. This parameter enables the servicegroup to process the LLM request/response based on the profile config. Any service item bound to the servicegroup will inherit the backend AIGW Profile bound at the servicegroup level, if it does not have an explicit AIGW Profile given at bind time.

##### `customserverid`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Unique service identifier. Used when the persistency type for the virtual server is set to Custom Server ID.

##### `dbsttl`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Specify the TTL for DNS record for domain based service.The default value of ttl is 0 which indicates to use the TTL received in DNS response for monitors

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Default value: `present`

##### `hashid`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[1]]`

Unique numerical identifier used by hash based load balancing methods to identify a service.

##### `monstate`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

Monitor state.

##### `nameserver`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Specify the nameserver to which the query for bound domain needs to be sent. If not specified, use the global nameserver

##### `order`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[1, 8192]]`

Order number to be assigned to the servicegroup member

##### `passive`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Indicates if load monitor is passive. A passive load monitor does not remove service from LB decision when threshold is breached.

##### `port`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[1, 65535]]`

Port number of the service. Each service must have a unique port number.

##### `serverid`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

The  identifier for the service. This is used when the persistency type is set to Custom Server ID.

##### `state`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

Initial state of the service after binding.

##### `weight`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[1, 100]]`

Weight to assign to the servers in the service group. Specifies the capacity of the servers relative to the other servers in the load balancing configuration. The higher the weight, the higher the percentage of requests sent to the service.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `nitro_servicegroup_lbmonitor_binding` type.

* [`servicegroupname`](#-nitro_servicegroup_lbmonitor_binding--servicegroupname)

Name of the service group.

### <a name="nitro_sslcertkey"></a>`nitro_sslcertkey`

Configuration for certificate key resource. Attributes map 1:1 onto the NITRO `sslcertkey` API, see the NITRO reference.
 Only attributes set in the manifest are managed.

The title is the NITRO `certkey`.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `nitro_sslcertkey` type.

##### `cert`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of and, optionally, path to the X509 certificate file that is used to form the certificate-key pair. The certificate file should be present on the appliance's hard-disk drive or solid-state drive. Storing a certificate in any location other than the default might cause inconsistency in a high availability setup. /nsconfig/ssl/ is the default path.

##### `deletecertkeyfilesonremoval`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['NO', 'ALWAYS', 'IF_EXPIRED']]`

This option is used to automatically delete certificate/key files from physical device when the added certkey is removed. When deleteCertKeyFilesOnRemoval option is used at rm certkey command, it overwrites the deleteCertKeyFilesOnRemoval setting used at add/set certkey command

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this resource should be present or absent on the NetScaler.

Default value: `present`

##### `expirymonitor`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

Issue an alert when the certificate is about to expire.

##### `fipskey`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of the FIPS key that was created inside the Hardware Security Module (HSM) of a FIPS appliance, or a key that was imported into the HSM.

##### `hsmkey`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of the HSM key that was created in the External Hardware Security Module (HSM) of a FIPS appliance.

##### `inform`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['DER', 'PEM', 'PFX']]`

Input format of the certificate and the private-key files. The three formats supported by the appliance are:\nPEM - Privacy Enhanced Mail\nDER - Distinguished Encoding Rule\nPFX - Personal Information Exchange

##### `key`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of and, optionally, path to the private-key file that is used to form the certificate-key pair. The certificate file should be present on the appliance's hard-disk drive or solid-state drive. Storing a certificate in any location other than the default might cause inconsistency in a high availability setup. /nsconfig/ssl/ is the default path.

##### `linkcertkeyname`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of the Certificate Authority certificate-key pair to which to link a certificate-key pair.

##### `notificationperiod`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[10, 100]]`

Time, in number of days, before certificate expiration, at which to generate an alert that the certificate is about to expire.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `nitro_sslcertkey` type.

* [`bundle`](#-nitro_sslcertkey--bundle)
* [`name`](#-nitro_sslcertkey--name)
* [`nodomaincheck`](#-nitro_sslcertkey--nodomaincheck)
* [`passplain`](#-nitro_sslcertkey--passplain)
* [`password`](#-nitro_sslcertkey--password)

##### <a name="-nitro_sslcertkey--bundle"></a>`bundle`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Parse the certificate chain as a single file after linking the server certificate to its issuer's certificate within the
file.

##### <a name="-nitro_sslcertkey--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `String`

Name for the certificate and private-key pair. Must begin with an ASCII alphanumeric or underscore (_) character, and
must contain only ASCII alphanumeric, underscore, hash (#), period (.), space, colon (:), at (@), equals (=), and hyphen
(-) characters. Cannot be changed after the certificate-key pair is created.\n\nThe following requirement applies only
to the Citrix ADC CLI:\nIf the name includes one or more spaces, enclose the name in double or single quotation marks
(for example, \"my cert\" or 'my cert'). (NITRO: `certkey`)

##### <a name="-nitro_sslcertkey--nodomaincheck"></a>`nodomaincheck`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Override the check for matching domain names during a certificate update operation.

##### <a name="-nitro_sslcertkey--passplain"></a>`passplain`

Data type: `Optional[Variant[String, Sensitive[String]]]`

Pass phrase used to encrypt the private-key. Required when adding an encrypted private-key in PEM format.

##### <a name="-nitro_sslcertkey--password"></a>`password`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Passphrase that was used to encrypt the private-key. Use this option to load encrypted private-keys in PEM format.

### <a name="nitro_sslvserver"></a>`nitro_sslvserver`

Configuration for SSL virtual server resource. Attributes map 1:1 onto the NITRO `sslvserver` API, see the NITRO reference.
 Only attributes set in the manifest are managed.

This entity cannot be created or deleted; it exists together with its parent and only its settings are managed.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `nitro_sslvserver` type.

##### `cipherredirect`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

State of Cipher Redirect. If cipher redirect is enabled, you can configure an SSL virtual server or service to display meaningful error messages if the SSL handshake fails because of a cipher mismatch between the virtual server or service and the client.

##### `cipherurl`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

The redirect URL to be used with the Cipher Redirect feature.

##### `cleartextport`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[0, 65534]]`

Port on which clear-text data is sent by the appliance to the server. Do not specify this parameter for SSL offloading with end-to-end encryption.

##### `clientauth`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

State of client authentication. If client authentication is enabled, the virtual server terminates the SSL handshake if the SSL client does not provide a valid certificate.

##### `clientcert`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['Mandatory', 'Optional']]`

Type of client authentication. If this parameter is set to MANDATORY, the appliance terminates the SSL handshake if the SSL client does not provide a valid certificate. With the OPTIONAL setting, the appliance requests a certificate from the SSL clients but proceeds with the SSL transaction even if the client presents an invalid certificate.\nCaution: Define proper access control policies before changing this setting to Optional.

##### `defaultsni`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Default domain name supported by the SSL virtual server. The parameter is effective, when zero touch certificate management is active for the SSL virtual server i.e. no manual SNI cert or default server cert is bound to the v-server.\nFor SSL transactions, when SNI is not presented by the client, server-certificate corresponding to the default SNI, if available in the cert-store, is selected else connection is terminated.

##### `dh`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

State of Diffie-Hellman (DH) key exchange.

##### `dhcount`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[0, 65534]]`

Number of interactions, between the client and the Citrix ADC, after which the DH private-public pair is regenerated. A value of zero (0) specifies refresh every time.

##### `dhekeyexchangewithpsk`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Whether or not the SSL Virtual Server will require a DHE key exchange to occur when a PSK is accepted during a TLS 1.3 resumption handshake.\nA DHE key exchange ensures forward secrecy even in the event that ticket keys are compromised, at the expense of an additional round trip and resources required to carry out the DHE key exchange.\nIf disabled, a DHE key exchange will be performed when a PSK is accepted but only if requested by the client.\nIf enabled, the server will require a DHE key exchange when a PSK is accepted regardless of whether the client supports combined PSK-DHE key exchange. This setting only has an effect when resumption is enabled.

##### `dhfile`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of and, optionally, path to the DH parameter file, in PEM format, to be installed. /nsconfig/ssl/ is the default path.

##### `dhkeyexpsizelimit`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

This option enables the use of NIST recommended (NIST Special Publication 800-56A) bit size for private-key size. For example, for DH params of size 2048bit, the private-key size recommended is 224bits. This is rounded-up to 256bits.

##### `dtls1`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

State of DTLSv1.0 protocol support for the SSL Virtual Server.

##### `dtls12`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

State of DTLSv1.2 protocol support for the SSL Virtual Server.

##### `dtlsprofilename`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of the DTLS profile whose settings are to be applied to the virtual server.

##### `ersa`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

State of Ephemeral RSA (eRSA) key exchange. Ephemeral RSA allows clients that support only export ciphers to communicate with the secure server even if the server certificate does not support export clients. The ephemeral RSA key is automatically generated when you bind an export cipher to an SSL or TCP-based SSL virtual server or service. When you remove the export cipher, the eRSA key is not deleted. It is reused at a later date when another export cipher is bound to an SSL or TCP-based SSL virtual server or service. The eRSA key is deleted when the appliance restarts.

##### `ersacount`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[0, 65534]]`

Refresh count for regeneration of the RSA public-key and private-key pair. Zero (0) specifies infinite usage (no refresh).

##### `hsts`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

State of HSTS protocol support for the SSL Virtual Server. Using HSTS, a server can enforce the use of an HTTPS connection for all communication with a client

##### `includesubdomains`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Enable HSTS for subdomains. If set to Yes, a client must send only HTTPS requests for subdomains.

##### `maxage`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[0, 4294967294]]`

Set the maximum time, in seconds, in the strict transport security (STS) header during which the client must send only HTTPS requests to the server

##### `ocspstapling`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

State of OCSP stapling support on the SSL virtual server. Supported only if the protocol used is higher than SSLv3. Possible values:\nENABLED: The appliance sends a request to the OCSP responder to check the status of the server certificate and caches the response for the specified time. If the response is valid at the time of SSL handshake with the client, the OCSP-based server certificate status is sent to the client during the handshake.\nDISABLED: The appliance does not check the status of the server certificate.

##### `preload`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Flag indicates the consent of the site owner to have their domain preloaded.

##### `pushenctrigger`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['Always', 'Merge', 'Ignore', 'Timer']]`

Trigger encryption on the basis of the PUSH flag value. Available settings function as follows:\n* ALWAYS - Any PUSH packet triggers encryption.\n* IGNORE - Ignore PUSH packet for triggering encryption.\n* MERGE - For a consecutive sequence of PUSH packets, the last PUSH packet triggers encryption.\n* TIMER - PUSH packet triggering encryption is delayed by the time defined in the set ssl parameter command or in the Change Advanced SSL Settings dialog box.

##### `redirectportrewrite`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

State of the port rewrite while performing HTTPS redirect. If this parameter is ENABLED and the URL from the server does not contain the standard port, the port is rewritten to the standard.

##### `sendclosenotify`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['YES', 'NO']]`

Enable sending SSL Close-Notify at the end of a transaction

##### `sessreuse`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

State of session reuse. Establishing the initial handshake requires CPU-intensive public key encryption operations. With the ENABLED setting, session key exchange is avoided for session resumption requests received from the client.

##### `sesstimeout`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[0, 4294967294]]`

Time, in seconds, for which to keep the session active. Any session resumption request received after the timeout period will require a fresh SSL handshake and establishment of a new SSL session.

##### `snienable`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

State of the Server Name Indication (SNI) feature on the virtual server and service-based offload. SNI helps to enable SSL encryption on multiple domains on a single virtual server or service if the domains are controlled by the same organization and share the same second-level domain name. For example, *.sports.net can be used to secure domains such as login.sports.net and help.sports.net.

##### `ssl2`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

State of SSLv2 protocol support for the SSL Virtual Server.

##### `ssl3`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

State of SSLv3 protocol support for the SSL Virtual Server.\nNote: On platforms with SSL acceleration chips, if the SSL chip does not support SSLv3, this parameter cannot be set to ENABLED.

##### `sslclientlogs`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

This parameter is used to enable or disable the logging of additional information, such as the Session ID and SNI names, from SSL handshakes to the audit logs.

##### `sslprofile`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of the SSL profile that contains SSL settings for the virtual server.

##### `sslredirect`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

State of HTTPS redirects for the SSL virtual server.\n\nFor an SSL session, if the client browser receives a redirect message, the browser tries to connect to the new location. However, the secure SSL session breaks if the object has moved from a secure site (https://) to an unsecure site (http://). Typically, a warning message appears on the screen, prompting the user to continue or disconnect.\nIf SSL Redirect is ENABLED, the redirect message is automatically converted from http:// to https:// and the SSL session does not break.

##### `sslv2redirect`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

State of SSLv2 Redirect. If SSLv2 redirect is enabled, you can configure an SSL virtual server or service to display meaningful error messages if the SSL handshake fails because of a protocol version mismatch between the virtual server or service and the client.

##### `sslv2url`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

URL of the page to which to redirect the client in case of a protocol version mismatch. Typically, this page has a clear explanation of the error or an alternative location that the transaction can continue from.

##### `strictclientekucheck`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

Enable strict EKU extension check during client authentication.

##### `strictsigdigestcheck`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

Parameter indicating to check whether peer entity certificate during TLS1.2 handshake is signed with one of signature-hash combination supported by Citrix ADC.

##### `tls1`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

State of TLSv1.0 protocol support for the SSL Virtual Server.

##### `tls11`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

State of TLSv1.1 protocol support for the SSL Virtual Server.

##### `tls12`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

State of TLSv1.2 protocol support for the SSL Virtual Server.

##### `tls13`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

State of TLSv1.3 protocol support for the SSL Virtual Server.

##### `tls13sessionticketsperauthcontext`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[1, 10]]`

Number of tickets the SSL Virtual Server will issue anytime TLS 1.3 is negotiated, ticket-based resumption is enabled, and either (1) a handshake completes or (2) post-handhsake client auth completes.\nThis value can be increased to enable clients to open multiple parallel connections using a fresh ticket for each connection.\nNo tickets are sent if resumption is disabled.

##### `zerorttearlydata`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']]`

State of TLS 1.3 0-RTT early data support for the SSL Virtual Server. This setting only has an effect if resumption is enabled, as early data cannot be sent along with an initial handshake.\nEarly application data has significantly different security properties - in particular there is no guarantee that the data cannot be replayed.

#### Parameters

namevar

Data type: `String`

Name of the SSL virtual server for which to set advanced configuration. (NITRO: `vservername`)

### <a name="nitro_sslvserver_sslcertkey_binding"></a>`nitro_sslvserver_sslcertkey_binding`

Binding Resource definition for describing association between sslvserver and sslcertkey resources Attributes map 1:1 onto the NITRO `sslvserver_sslcertkey_binding` API, see the NITRO reference.
 Only attributes set in the manifest are managed.

The title is split into `vservername`, `certkeyname`.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `nitro_sslvserver_sslcertkey_binding` type.

##### `ca`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

CA certificate.

##### `crlcheck`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['Mandatory', 'Optional']]`

The state of the CRL check parameter. (Mandatory/Optional)

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this resource should be present or absent on the NetScaler.

Default value: `present`

##### `ocspcheck`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['Mandatory', 'Optional']]`

The state of the OCSP check parameter. (Mandatory/Optional)

##### `skipcaname`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

The flag is used to indicate whether this particular CA certificate's CA_Name needs to be sent to the SSL client while requesting for client certificate in a SSL handshake

##### `snicert`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

The name of the CertKey. Use this option to bind Certkey(s) which will be used in SNI processing.

The name of the certificate key pair binding.
